goal: i wanna increase my font size
preamble: Font size feels like a number you have to know in advance — 12, 14, 18 — and most people open the size box and guess. But you rarely want a specific number; you want the text a bit bigger than it is now. Docs has a control for exactly that: a nudge, one notch at a time, with the page in front of you while you do it. One more thing before you start: size applies to whatever is selected. Select the text you want to grow first, or if nothing is selected, the change waits for whatever you type next.
generalization: Anywhere you see a number box flanked by a minus and a plus, you're being offered two ways to work: name the value, or adjust it by eye. Naming it is faster when you know what you want; nudging is better when you don't, because you get to judge each step against the thing itself. Font size, zoom, line spacing, image dimensions — the stepper is always there for the times you'd otherwise be guessing.

steps.intent: This is the plus beside the font size box, and each click moves the selection up one step on the size ladder Docs uses. You are not setting a size, you are raising it — which means you can watch the text and stop when it looks right, instead of deciding on a number and then living with it. Notice the box itself tick over as you click.
hints: Size is a property of text, so it sits with the other text controls rather than in a menu. Look for something that changes a value by a step rather than asking you to name one.
In the toolbar, the small number box right of the font name — the plus on its right-hand side.

wrongHints.Font size: That opens the number itself, which does work — but it asks you to pick a size before you can see it. The plus beside it makes the same change one notch at a time, so you can judge by eye.
wrongHints.Decrease font size: Same control, opposite direction — that one is the minus. They sit either side of the number box, so it is an easy pair to mix up. The plus is on the right.
wrongHints.Font: That changes the typeface — which letterforms are used. The size is a separate property, and it lives in the box just to the right.
wrongHints.Bold: Bold makes text heavier, not larger. It is a common stand-in for emphasis, but it will not change the size at all.
wrongHints.Styles: Styles set size as part of a larger package — heading, subtitle, normal text. Useful when you want meaning as well as size, but here you only want the text bigger.
